instruction.name: armrrx.w
instruction.description: ARM-style rotate right extended on 32-bit values.

experiments.name: flags read-write loop
experiments.init: li.d $r12, 5; li.d $r13, 7; li.d $r4, 9; li.d $r5, 11; li.d $r6, 13; li.d $r7, 15; x86mtflag $r12, 0x3f; armmtflag $r12, 0x39
experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 20000 --unroll2 40000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 10 --init 'li.d $r12, 5; li.d $r13, 7; li.d $r4, 9; li.d $r5, 11; li.d $r6, 13; li.d $r7, 15; x86mtflag $r12, 0x3f; armmtflag $r12, 0x39' --asm 'armrrx.w $r12, 14'

latencies.notes: EFLAGS -> EFLAGS: the instruction reads and writes the flag register, so one copy already forms a chain and the measured 2.00 cycles are the read-modify-write path. An earlier chain appended `x86mtflag rd, mask`, but these instructions write no GPR, so that pair had no dependency and only reported the length of a dependency-free sequence.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.notes: rd -> ARMFLAGS chain closed by armmfflag; 1 cycle subtracted.

latencies.notes: rd -> ARMFLAGS chain closed by armmfflag; 1 cycle subtracted. Raw slope-method measurement was 3.01; the nominal value is 3 cycle(s).

notes: LBT ARM-style instruction. Latency is recorded for each source operand: ARMFLAGS -> ARMFLAGS (2), rj -> ARMFLAGS (3). Only ARMFLAGS is written: the general-purpose registers are read-only sources for this instruction (verified with a native test program, where armadd.w, armsub.w, armand.w, armmov.w, armrotr.w and armrrx.w leave every GPR unchanged while ARMFLAGS changes; the conditional move armMove is the exception and does write its destination). Throughput is not measurable for this instruction: it reads and writes the architectural flag register, so every copy depends on the flags written by the previous one and a body of copies is a dependency chain, not a set of independent lanes. Eight copies take 16 cycles, which is exactly the 2-cycle read-modify-write latency, so the only number that can be quoted is that a stream of flag-modifying instructions runs at one per two cycles. The `throughput` array is therefore empty; see the latency entry from EFLAGS to EFLAGS.
